gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Nordic spaces its letters out like brush dabs set far apart, each one a single unvarying line with a tightly folded opening. And Noto Sans Gurmukhi follows with outward-pointing terminals and low contrast, so paragraphs move along quietly.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Ancient and sparse, Nordic draws every letter as one thread of ink with no tilt to its rounds, while Noto Sans Hanunoo fills the line with tall lowercase. Text moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Nordic is a thread of ink with no swelling or tapering, letters scattered wide like dabs of a brush. But Noto Sans Hebrew packs a dominant midsection into each line, with wide gaps where curves meet stems, so long text stays easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-hk: Pressed-leaf tight and sternly ancient, Nordic keeps its letters closed up. And Noto Sans HK lifts its brush ends away before curves finish, giving the page a loose counterpoint to that folded heading.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-imperial-: Bent copper pipe, basically: Nordic runs tubular strokes. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic sits beneath with a c whose ends point apart like open pincers, so the heavy ancient heading gets a friendly, low-contrast partner.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-inscripti: Nordic closes its letters up tight, like leaves pressed shut, each drawn with one unvarying stroke. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian answers by opening every e and a wide, and that closed-versus-open tension is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP reads with a very tall x-height and curves that sweep open instead of curling shut. Noto Sans JP handles running text, while Nordic does its best work as a line of constant weight tracing powerful, ancient letters.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals give Noto Sans Kaithi a sturdy, open feel, with a channel running through each e. But Nordic is better at stopping the eye with no thick-and-thin contrast, while Noto Sans Kaithi is better at carrying it onward.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Nordic cuts its letters like a fixed-width router bit, closed, powerful and ancient, spaced far apart across the line. Its partner Noto Sans Kannada opens up wide.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li lifts its brush ends away before the curves close, and its capitals sit only slightly above the lowercase. And Nordic, closed and ancient, gives that gentle text a heavy-handed headline.
